Elena — thanks, I got the attachments and shared them with Procurement, Finance and Legal. Quick next steps from our side:

- Procurement (me) will create the vendor record in our system once Finance confirms tax classification.
- Finance (Rishi) will confirm whether we can route invoices net under reverse-charge or need grossed-up invoices.
- Legal (Priyom) will confirm if we need a signed tax residency attestation clause in the master services agreement or PO.

To speed things up, can you also confirm:
- Primary invoice email (e.g., finance@astralogix.nl) and invoice billing address (must match KvK extract).
- Do you accept 60-day NET? (Redwood standard is 30 by default; we can confirm timing in PO)

I’ve included a short evidence matrix below of what usually clears vendor onboarding in EU cases — finance/legal, please correct/add:

Required for vendor record:
- Company registry extract (KvK) — establishes legal entity name and registered address
- VAT registration certificate — VAT ID for cross-border invoicing
- Certificate of Fiscal Residency (or equivalent) — to support non-US withholding/refund positions
- Invoice remit details (email, IBAN, SWIFT)

Optional/conditional:
- Apostille or legalized translation (if red flags)
- Signed attestation re: withholding responsibilities (if Redwood required to withhold)

Once Finance confirms classification we’ll generate a tentative PO number and share payment terms.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: AstraLogix tax residency docs attached

Looping in a quick legal view. The documents Elena provided look standard; a couple of notes: 

- Reverse-charge: If AstraLogix is supplying services from the Netherlands to Redwood EU entities, reverse-charge typically applies and Redwood should not withhold VAT. We need to confirm which Redwood legal entity will be billed (US vs EU).
- Withholding: For payments from a Redwood US legal entity, W-8 forms are not applicable for EU corporate vendors — instead we rely on local tax residency docs and intercompany invoicing rules.

If Procurement wants a short signed attestation we can add the following clause to the PO or MSA before first payment: 

"Vendor certifies that it is a taxable person under the laws of its jurisdiction and that the invoices submitted to Redwood for cross-border services are subject to local VAT rules and, where applicable, reverse-charge. Vendor will provide a certificate of fiscal residency upon request and notify Redwood of any change in tax residency status."

If Finance confirms that Redwood should treat invoices net, Procurement can proceed with vendor setup. If payments originate from Redwood US and taxes could be withheld by payer, we’ll need to discuss gross-up language.

- Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: AstraLogix tax residency docs attached

All — reviewed AstraLogix docs. VAT number matches KvK registry and certificate. Action items from Finance: 

1) Treat as EU supplier — apply reverse-charge when billed to Redwood EU entity. No withholding expected for EU-to-EU services.
2) If Redwood US entity is invoiced, Treasury needs to check treaty application; likely no US withholding but we should request invoice with VAT net and include invoice-level VAT note.
3) Please have vendor confirm remit details (IBAN + SWIFT). We need vendor banking to create payment profile.

Procurement: you can create the vendor record pending receipt of remit details. I recommend PO terms: Net 30, EUR, PO to reference vendor VAT ID, and include the attestation clause Priyom suggested in the PO notes.

I’ll mark this vendor as "EU VAT-validated — reverse charge eligible" in our system so accounting posts correctly.

Rishi Malhotra
